toGuest.value: Eggs Hussarde is New Orleans’ answer to Eggs Benedict, with a red wine sauce as well as hollandaise.
Eggs Sardou is the New Orleans egg dish with artichokes and creamed spinach.
Marchand de vin is a savory red wine and mushroom sauce; it gives the eggs a deep, rich note.
Hollandaise is the buttery, lemony egg-yolk sauce you know from Eggs Benedict.
Béarnaise is a rich butter sauce with tarragon, the classic sauce for steak.
Choron is a béarnaise with tomato, tangy and herbal.
Sauce Foyot is béarnaise made even richer with a reduced beef glaze.
Débris is meltingly tender, slow-cooked meat in its own gravy.
Véronique means fish with grapes, ours are pickled with hibiscus.
En papillote means in paper; here we use a banana leaf instead, so the fish steams in its own juices and stays moist.
Beurre blanc is a silky white wine and butter sauce.
Poussin à la moutarde means young chicken with mustard.
’Nduja is a spicy, spreadable Italian sausage that melts into the beans.
Persillade is a fresh parsley-and-garlic topping, ours has pumpkin seeds for crunch.
Mignonette is the classic raw bar sauce for oysters, vinegar, shallot and cracked pepper; ours has preserved Fresno chili.
The egg yolk is cured and grated over the top, like bottarga, it adds a rich, salty finish.
Brabant potatoes are New Orleans’ crispy cubed potatoes.
Milk punch is our classic breakfast cocktail: brandy, cream, vanilla and nutmeg.
A Bloody Bull is a Bloody Mary with beef broth, savory and rich.
Chicory is a roasted root we blend into our coffee, the New Orleans way.
Café brûlot is New Orleans’ spiced, flamed coffee, the cake borrows its flavors.

say.value: TAH-so (TASS-oh is also heard; confirm the house habit)

toGuest.value: Tasso is Cajun spiced, cured and smoked pork, used to season the sauce.
Popcorn rice is a Louisiana rice with a nutty, toasty aroma.
Tarte Tatin is the French upside-down caramelized tart, ours is pineapple.

say.value: ERB-sant (ERB-saint also heard); never sound the H

toGuest.value: Herbsaint is the anise liqueur created in New Orleans in 1934, just a rinse in the Sazerac glass for aroma.
Framboise is French for raspberry; the French toast is finished with raspberry coulis and local raspberries.
Fines herbes is the classic French mix of delicate herbs, parsley, chives, tarragon and chervil, on the crab claws.
Mimolette is a bright orange French cheese from Lille, nutty and a little sweet as it ages, dyed with annatto; it makes the fondue on the shells and cheese.
Pralines are the New Orleans pecan and brown sugar candies crumbled over the bread pudding.
Rösti is the Swiss grated potato cake under the petite filet on the breakfast tasting.
Mascarpone is a rich Italian cream cheese, whipped into a light mousse for the French toast.
Shiitake are the savory Japanese mushrooms, preserved, on the blackened tofu.
Burrata is fresh mozzarella with a creamy center, on the Creole tomato tostada.
Grana Padano is a hard, nutty Italian cheese like Parmesan, on the Caesar and the shells and cheese.
Castelvetrano olives are the bright green, mild and buttery Sicilian olives in the papillote.
Gremolata is a fresh chopped topping; ours is Marcona almond with lemon and basil on the crab and corn omelette.
Harissa is the North African chili paste that seasons the smoked cauliflower.
Yuzu is a fragrant Japanese citrus; its mousse is the heart of the lemon tart.
Chateaubriand is the thick center cut of the beef tenderloin, roasted for two.
Confit is meat cured and cooked slowly in its own fat until tender; the duck leg on the waffle.
Pavé means paving stone; the smoked potato pavé is layered potato pressed and cut into a neat block.
Andouille is the smoky Louisiana pork sausage in the gumbo.
Gumbo is the Louisiana stew built on a dark roux; ours is seafood with andouille over popcorn rice.
Luxardo is the Italian family house famous for maraschino cherries and the liqueur, founded in 1821 and in Italy since 1947; its sauce dresses the Cherries Jubilee.

Peychaud's is the bright red New Orleans bitters with anise and cherry notes in the Sazerac; the story puts Antoine Peychaud's pharmacy a few doors up Royal Street, so confirm it at lineup before telling it.
The Sazerac is New Orleans' official cocktail: ours is rye stirred with Peychaud's in a glass rinsed with Herbsaint, and the first Sazeracs were made on Cognac, as our Origin Story is.
Crème fraîche is a slightly tangy cultured cream, sweetened on the baked apple and whipped on the coffee cake.
Financiers are small, buttery almond cakes; the blackberry ones give the trifle its texture.
A bavarois, or Bavarian, is a set cream; the Snickers starts with a Bavarian milk chocolate.
Paul Blangé was the house's first chef, who led the kitchen until the 1970s and created Bananas Foster and Eggs Hussarde.
Escoffier was the great French chef who wrote down sauce Foyot and made Cherries Jubilee for Queen Victoria.
The guéridon is the cart the Bananas Foster is made on at your table.
Fresno is a red Californian chili from the 1950s, about the heat of a jalapeño but fruitier; preserved in the mignonette it gives a gentle warmth, not real heat.
Creole is New Orleans city cooking, French and Spanish at the root with more butter, cream and sauces; Cajun is the country cooking of Acadiana, one pot, dark roux and spicier. Brennan's is Creole.

say.value: As it reads: Piper-Heidsieck (no research respelling; ask the sommelier)

toGuest.value: Piper-Heidsieck is the Champagne house behind our house bubbles, bottled under the Brennan's name as an Extra Brut, very dry.
Rare is the prestige vintage Champagne that began at Piper-Heidsieck and is now its own house; we pour it by the glass from a bottle kept fresh under a Coravin Sparkling stopper.
Pierre Sparr is an Alsace house; its sparkling rosé is all Pinot Noir, made like Champagne, dry with bright berry fruit.
Charles Lafitte is the crisp, dry Champagne poured on both tasting menus, a house with roots to 1834 in the Vranken-Pommery group.
C.H. Berres is an old Mosel family estate at Ürzig; its Old Vines Riesling is our off-dry glass for spice and for the duck waffle.
Pazo das Bruxas, the manor of the witches, is Familia Torres's Albariño from Spain's Atlantic coast, citrusy with a salty edge.

say.value: As it reads: Albariño (no research respelling; ask the sommelier)

toGuest.value: Albariño is the crisp, saline white grape of Rías Baixas in Galicia, made for seafood.
Durand is the family behind our Loire Sauvignon Blanc, crisp and herbal, the wine that loves artichokes; the current menu prints it as Famille Durand.

say.value: GAY-nee (worth an ear check with the sommelier)

toGuest.value: Gainey is a Santa Barbara County estate; its Chardonnay is creamy but fresh, our first pick for the butter sauces.
Domaine Leflaive is one of Burgundy's great white wine estates, famous for Puligny-Montrachet; we pour its Mâcon by the glass by Coravin.
Mâcon-Verzé is the village appellation in southern Burgundy where Leflaive makes this Chardonnay.
Domaine Fichet is a family estate at Igé in the Mâconnais; its Château London is a named vineyard parcel, no castle and nothing to do with England.
Mâcon-Igé is the village appellation of the Fichet Chardonnay poured with the lobster on the dinner tasting.
Minuty is a Provence estate; its Prestige rosé is pale, dry and refreshing, lovely with tomatoes and shrimp.
Damien Martin runs his family's domaine at Davayé in the Mâconnais; his Bourgogne Pinot Noir is our light, silky red by the glass.
Louis Jadot is the Burgundy house whose Beaune Premier Cru is poured with the redfish on the dinner tasting; Beaune has no Grand Cru, so Premier Cru is its top tier.
Beaune is the wine capital of Burgundy and the village behind the Jadot Premier Cru on the tasting.
Beaumes-de-Venise is a Southern Rhône village famous for sweet Muscat; the Durban we pour is its dry red, ripe Grenache with Syrah.
Domaine de Durban is the Beaumes-de-Venise estate behind our ripe, soft Southern Rhône red.
Domaine de Châteaumar makes the Cuvée Vincent Côtes du Rhône poured with the filet at breakfast: old vine Syrah from beside Châteauneuf-du-Pape, juicy and soft.
Moulin d'Issan is the Bordeaux from the Château d'Issan team in Margaux, a Cabernet Sauvignon blend, cassis and cedar for the steak.
Rubicon is Inglenook's flagship Napa Cabernet from Rutherford; our 2010 has sixteen years of age, powerful but silky, $70 the glass.
Paul Hobbs is the Napa winemaker whose Coombsville Cabernet is poured with the duck on the dinner tasting.
Coombsville is one of Napa's cooler corners, near the town of Napa, so its Cabernet keeps its freshness.
Dr. Hermann is the Mosel estate behind our sweet Erdener Prälat Auslese, the $80 half-bottle for dessert.
Erdener Prälat is one of the Mosel's famous steep vineyards, the source of our Auslese.
Auslese means selected harvest, a tier above late harvest Spätlese: sweet, honeyed Riesling with bright acidity.
La Tour Vieille is the Banyuls estate whose Reserva, fig, caramel and coffee, is the dessert pour on the dinner tasting.
Banyuls is a sweet fortified red from the schist terraces of Roussillon, at least half Grenache, the classic with chocolate.
Coravin lets us pour a single glass and keep the bottle fresh: a needle through the cork for the Leflaive, a sparkling stopper on the opened bottle for the Rare.
Extra Brut means under six grams of sugar a liter, very dry; our house Champagne is one.
Creekstone Farms is Black Angus beef from a Kansas producer; the breakfast hanger is USDA Prime.
Vital Farms is pasture raised eggs; every hen gets over a hundred square feet of grass.
Rohan is a special cross bred for the D'Artagnan company and raised in New York's Hudson Valley for tender, rosy meat.

say.value: As it reads: D'Artagnan (no research respelling; ask the kitchen)

toGuest.value: D'Artagnan is the New York purveyor that raises the Rohan duck; do not volunteer the name unless asked.
Rice grits are the broken grains from Two Brooks Farm at Sumner in the Mississippi Delta, a family rice farm since 1992; not Louisiana.
The tofu is made across the river by Tien Dat, a Vietnamese family co-op, pressed fresh every week.
The Caesar's crisps are made from Leidenheimer, the po-boy bread of New Orleans since 1896.
Nueske's is the Wisconsin bacon famous for real applewood smoke, since 1933; it is in the succotash.
Abita Amber is the Louisiana lager from Abita Springs, brewed since 1986; it goes into the Mimolette fondue on the shells and cheese.
Tullamore D.E.W. is the Irish whiskey in our Irish Coffee; the initials are the founder's, Daniel E. Williams.
Lyre's is an Australian non-alcoholic spirit, labeled under 0.5 percent alcohol; its agave is in the Oh! What It Seemed to Be.

say.value: As it reads: Grand Isle Jewel.

toGuest.value: Grand Isle Jewels are oysters farmed in floating cages off Grand Isle, a brand launched in 2025 by the island's growers; the menu's singular Jewel is the plural brand.
Our mushroom side; the kitchen says which mushrooms and how they are cooked tonight.
Congregation Coffee roasts in Algiers, across the river; read tonight's single origin from the coffee card rather than naming it from memory.
Lillet Blanc is a light French aperitif wine, floral and citrusy; it is in the To Each His Own and, at Bubbles, the Riviera.
Monkey 47 is a Black Forest gin bottled at 47 percent, with a big botanical lift; it goes into the Flamingo.
Chopin is a Polish potato vodka, smooth and round; it goes into the Flamingo.
Taittinger is one of the great Champagne houses; its La Française is the Champagne in the Flamingo.
Rabbit Hole Dareringer is a Kentucky straight bourbon from Louisville, finished in PX sherry casks; it is the base of the Birdcage.
Cap Corse Mattei Blanc is a Corsican quinquina, a wine aperitif with a gentle bitterness; it goes into the Spoonbill.
A quinquina is a wine aperitif with a gentle bitterness, from the same bark that gives tonic water its bite.
Hendrick's is a Scottish gin with cucumber and rose; it is the base of the Spoonbill.
Willett is a family distillery in Bardstown, Kentucky, founded in 1936; its 4-year rye makes Thompson's Dream.
Dudognon is a family Cognac estate in Grande Champagne, Cognac's first growth; it is the base of Origin Story.
Jade Nouvelle-Orléans is an absinthe created by a New Orleans native as a tribute to the city's nineteenth century absinthe houses; it is in Origin Story.
St. George Absinthe Verte, from California, was the first American absinthe made legally after the 1912 ban; it rinses the glass for Thompson's Dream.
The Bitter Truth is a bitters maker from Munich; its Creole Bitters are a tribute to the New Orleans style, built for the Sazerac.
Café glacé is French for iced coffee; ours is chicory cold brew with cardamom-clove syrup and orange flower foam.
Rémoulade is a tangy, herby sauce for dipping; ours carries chives and comes with the crawfish meat pies.
Angostura is the classic aromatic bitters of an Old Fashioned; it goes into the Birdcage.
Calvados is apple brandy from northern France; Daron Fine Calvados is the base of To Each His Own.
Green Chartreuse is a French herbal liqueur, green, intense and high in alcohol; it goes into Five Minutes More.
Licor 43 is a Spanish liqueur that tastes of vanilla and citrus; it rounds out Five Minutes More.
Volcán Reposado is a tequila rested in oak, rounder than an unaged one; it is the base of Old Buttermilk Sky.
Amarula is a South African cream liqueur made with the fruit of the marula tree; it floats in Floating in South Africa.
Frangelico is an Italian hazelnut liqueur; it goes into the Espresso Martini and Ralph’s Coffee.
Nocello is an Italian walnut liqueur; it goes into Ralph’s Coffee.
Pedro Ximénez is the sweetest style of sherry, dark and syrupy, made from the grape of that name; it goes into the Banane au Chocolat.
Wölffer Estate makes the zero proof sparkling rosé in the Personality; confirm the label’s alcohol figure with the bar.
Reposado means rested: a tequila aged in oak for a while, rounder and softer than an unaged one.

scenarios.title: First breakfast
scenarios.guest: It’s our first time, what’s the real Brennan’s breakfast?

you.value: Welcome! The classic is a Brandy Milk Punch to start, our Turtle Soup, Eggs Hussarde, and Bananas Foster flambéed right here at the table. If you’d like all of it in one go, our Traditional Breakfast is $80 and includes tasting portions and every drink on it.

principle.value: Sell the ritual, then offer the tasting as the easy yes.

scenarios.title: Foster for one
scenarios.guest: Just me, can I get the Bananas Foster?

you.value: It’s made in one pan at the table for at least two people, so the minimum order is two. If you’d like a flambé just for you, let me ask the manager what the kitchen can do tonight. And for something sweet in a glass, the Banane au Chocolat is banana and chocolate with Pedro Ximénez sherry, a dessert cocktail for one, $16.00.

principle.value: Explain the reason for the rule, then offer an alternative with the same theater, and check before you promise. Cherries Jubilee is not on the current dessert menu: confirm with a manager that it is served, and whether a single order is possible, before you mention it.

scenarios.title: No alcohol
scenarios.guest: We don’t drink. Can we still have the Bananas Foster? Doesn’t the alcohol burn off?

you.value: Some of it burns off, but most of it stays, so I wouldn’t recommend it if you avoid alcohol completely. The Lemon Tart or the Pineapple Tarte Tatin are wonderful, and for a drink, our spirit-free Personality is zero proof sparkling rosé with tart cherry juice, $16.00.

principle.value: Be accurate about alcohol; never promise it ‘all cooks off.’ Also watch the turtle soup (Sherry), bread pudding (whiskey caramel) and shells & cheese (beer).

scenarios.title: Vegetarian at dinner
scenarios.guest: I’m vegetarian. What can I have?

you.value: The Creole Tomato Tostada to start, then the Blackened Tofu, it’s local Tien Dat tofu with rice grits and shiitakes, and the Smoked Cauliflower on the side. Let me confirm with the kitchen about butter and stocks. At breakfast: Eggs Sardou or the Framboise French Toast, with the same check.

principle.value: Name a full meal, then verify the hidden animal products (butter, stock, gelatin, bouillon in the Bloody Bull, bacon in the succotash).

scenarios.title: Shellfish allergy
scenarios.guest: I’m allergic to shellfish.

you.value: Thank you for telling me. I’m writing it on the ticket and the chef will go through your choices with me. Where the menu lists shellfish: on both menus, the gumbo and the Creole Caesar’s smoked oyster dressing; at breakfast and lunch, the Louisiana Oysters, the Pecan Gulf Fish with crab, the Crab & Corn Omelette and the Shrimp & Grits; at dinner, the Grand Isle Jewel Oysters, the Louisiana Crab Claws, the Gulf Fish en Papillote with crab, and the Louisiana BBQ Lobster on the tasting. Give me two minutes and I’ll come back with what the chef is happy to send.

principle.value: Name what the menu prints, never what is probably fine; the kitchen clears the dish, not you; flag the ticket and tell the captain.

scenarios.title: Chateaubriand wine
scenarios.guest: We’re sharing the Chateaubriand. What should we drink?

you.value: Two directions: by the glass, the 2010 Inglenook Rubicon: Napa Cabernet with sixteen years of age, so it’s powerful but silky, $70. Or, for elegance, a red Burgundy from our cellar, I’d love to bring our sommelier over to pick one with you.

principle.value: Give two styles and a clear price, and use the cellar and sommelier as a resource.

scenarios.title: Celebration
scenarios.guest: It’s our anniversary, something special to start?

you.value: Congratulations! We pour a prestige vintage Champagne by the glass: Rare, kept fresh under a Coravin stopper, at $75. For something lighter, our house Piper-Heidsieck Extra Brut. And if you’re here on a Friday at 5, we saber Champagne in the courtyard.

principle.value: Match the moment with a special pour and a Brennan’s ritual. Check the vintage and the sabering schedule before you say either.

scenarios.title: Shellfish and nuts at one table
scenarios.guest: My husband is allergic to shellfish and I’m allergic to tree nuts.

you.value: Thank you both. It goes on the ticket and the chef walks through your choices with me before I promise anything. The menu lists shellfish in the gumbo, the Caesar dressing, the oysters, the crab dishes and the shrimp; and nuts in the pecan fish, the omelette, the papillote, the duck and the coffee cake. Two minutes with the kitchen.

principle.value: Name what is printed, let the kitchen give the final answer, flag the ticket, tell the captain.

scenarios.title: Pregnant guest and raw oysters
scenarios.guest: I’m pregnant. Are the oysters OK?

you.value: The Grand Isle oysters are served raw, and the menu carries the advisory that raw shellfish carries a risk, especially in pregnancy. I can’t advise you medically, so that’s your call. For the same brininess cooked, the Crab Claws come warm in brown butter, and at breakfast the Louisiana Oysters are cooked in BBQ sauce.

principle.value: State the advisory, never decide for the guest, never moralize, have a cooked alternative ready.

scenarios.title: Vegan at breakfast
scenarios.guest: I’m vegan. What can I have?

you.value: Honestly, our breakfast is built on eggs and butter, so I won’t guess. The chef can usually build something and I’d rather ask her than improvise. Grits, Brabant potatoes and the fruit starters are where she usually starts, and every one needs a question about butter or dairy.

principle.value: Honesty, then the kitchen, never a guessed plate.

scenarios.title: Gluten
scenarios.guest: I avoid gluten.

you.value: The obvious ones are the English muffins, the biscuit, the French toast and the bread pudding. Where it hides I won’t guess: the soups may be roux based, the artichokes and the grit cake are fried, and the fryer and the blackening spice need a question. Let me have the kitchen go through it with me.

principle.value: Separate the obvious from the hidden; send the hidden to the kitchen.

scenarios.title: A child at the table
scenarios.guest: Anything for a six-year-old?

you.value: Yes, our children's menu is for ten and under, $25.00 for three courses with a drink. If she likes things plain, the grilled cheese or the buttered noodles; at breakfast, the vanilla French toast with berries and whipped cream. I'll put her order in first so it comes out quickly, and when the Bananas Foster is lit she'll love it from her seat; we keep little ones back from the cart.

principle.value: Child's order in first and out fast; cart distance; make the flame a treat. Read from the children's card for the meal and confirm today's kid's drink.

scenarios.title: Creole versus Cajun
scenarios.guest: What’s the difference between Creole and Cajun?

you.value: Creole is New Orleans city cooking: French and Spanish at the root, African and Caribbean hands in it, more butter, cream and tomato, more sauces. Cajun is the country cooking of Acadiana, from the Acadian exiles, one pot, dark roux, rustic and spicier. Brennan’s is Creole. You’ll hear me say Cajun for a few ingredients, like the tasso in the shrimp and grits.

principle.value: Two sentences, then back to the menu.

scenarios.title: The tourist who wants the one thing
scenarios.guest: We’re here once. What do we order?

you.value: At breakfast, the Traditional Breakfast at $80 is the whole story: milk punch, baked apple, turtle soup or gumbo with a Bloody Bull, Eggs Hussarde, a petite filet, and Bananas Foster at the table, drinks included. À la carte, it’s the Turtle Soup, the Eggs Hussarde and the Bananas Foster for two.

principle.value: One clear answer, then a shorter one.

scenarios.title: Bananas Foster alone, at dinner
scenarios.guest: I’m dining alone and I came for the Bananas Foster.

you.value: You came to the right place. It’s made in one pan for two, so the order is for two; that’s the pan, not a rule about company. If you’d like a flame for one, I’ll ask the manager what the kitchen can do tonight, and the Banane au Chocolat, banana and chocolate with Pedro Ximénez sherry, is a dessert cocktail for one, $16.00.

principle.value: The reason, the same theater, check before promising, a small consolation. Cherries Jubilee is off the current dessert menu: check with a manager before you mention it.

scenarios.title: A cheaper bottle for the Chateaubriand
scenarios.guest: Seventy dollars a glass is more than we want to spend.

you.value: Absolutely. The Moulin d’Issan Bordeaux at $16 has the cassis and cedar for the beef, and the Durban Southern Rhône at $19.00 is riper and softer. For a bottle, let me bring our sommelier with the list; tell her roughly where you’d like to land and she’ll find the best value there.

principle.value: Two prices from the list, then the list and the sommelier; never a bottle price from memory; the guest names the budget privately.

scenarios.title: In a hurry before a tour
scenarios.guest: We have a swamp tour at one. Can we be out in forty-five minutes?

you.value: Yes, if we order now and I put the whole table in at once. I’d steer you to the egg dishes and the soup rather than the Chateaubriand or the flambé today, and I’ll bring the check with your last course.

principle.value: Ask the clock, set the pace, tell the kitchen, bring the check early.

scenarios.title: A birthday
scenarios.guest: It’s my mother’s birthday.

you.value: Happy birthday to her. A little fuss, or something quieter? I can pour her a glass of the Rare Champagne to start, and the Bananas Foster is made at the table for the two of you, which is the best candle we have.

principle.value: Loud or quiet first; note it on the ticket.

scenarios.title: Turtle soup too rich
scenarios.guest: This is too rich for me.

you.value: I’m sorry, that’s on me for not saying how rich it is. Let me take it away. The gumbo is lighter and brinier, or the Creole Caesar if you’d like something crisp. Either is on me to swap.

principle.value: The five A’s: awareness, acknowledgement, apology, action, additional generosity (Danny Meyer, Setting the Table, 2006). Tell the manager so the comp is recorded.

scenarios.title: A wine sent back
scenarios.guest: This doesn’t taste right.

you.value: Thank you for saying so. I’ll take it away and bring a fresh glass, or something different if you’d prefer. Shall I bring our sommelier to taste it with you?

principle.value: Never debate a send back; tell the sommelier so a faulty by the glass bottle is pulled before it reaches another table.

scenarios.title: A Sazerac on the rocks
scenarios.guest: Sazerac on the rocks, please.

you.value: Of course. The classic here is served without ice in a chilled glass rinsed with Herbsaint, so it stays spirit forward; over ice it softens as it sits. Let me ask the bar to build it on a large cube for you.

principle.value: Say the classic once, then make the guest’s drink the guest’s way. The over ice build is expert knowledge, not the guide’s; the guide tells you to confirm the bar’s build, so ask.

scenarios.title: Ketchup with the Brabant potatoes
scenarios.guest: Could I get some ketchup for the potatoes?

you.value: Of course, right away.

principle.value: A ramekin, without a flicker.

scenarios.title: Is the tofu vegan?
scenarios.guest: Is the Blackened Tofu vegan?

you.value: Good question, and I’d rather check than guess. Blackening is traditionally done with butter, and I want to confirm the rice grits are cooked without stock. One moment with the kitchen.

principle.value: The guide flags exactly these two questions; defer every time.

scenarios.title: Is Eggs Owen for Owen Brennan?
scenarios.guest: Is Eggs Owen named after Owen Brennan?

you.value: Owen Brennan founded the restaurant in 1946, so it’s a fair guess, but the menu doesn’t say and I’d rather not invent it. What I can tell you is the plate: short rib braised in red wine, a Creole spiced potato and a soft boiled egg with both sauces.

principle.value: Never an unconfirmed house story; pivot to the plate.

scenarios.title: Dress code for tonight
scenarios.guest: My son only has shorts with him.

you.value: Our dinner code is dressy casual, jackets preferred, and we ask guests to avoid athletic or cut-off shorts, sleeveless or decal T-shirts, hats and open-toed shoes for men. Let me ask the manager what’s workable tonight so there’s no surprise at the door.

principle.value: Say the code, hand enforcement to the host stand.

scenarios.title: One tasting, one à la carte
scenarios.guest: I’ll do the tasting menu and she’ll order à la carte. Does that work?

you.value: Let me check with the kitchen on tonight’s pacing; a tasting runs five courses and I want your plates to land with them. The Chateaubriand isn’t ideal for a split table because it’s for two.

principle.value: Pacing is a kitchen question; protect both guests from waiting.

scenarios.title: Is the gumbo hot?
scenarios.guest: Is the gumbo spicy?

you.value: Mild to moderate: smoky andouille and a gentle warmth, not heat. I can bring hot sauce, or if you’re spice shy the turtle soup has none.

principle.value: The guide’s spice words, and both directions.

scenarios.title: The sabering
scenarios.guest: You cut Champagne open with a sword?

you.value: We do, in the courtyard, during Bubbles at Brennan’s; the guide says Fridays at 5. It’s a bar team ritual, so be in the courtyard a few minutes early. Rosé bottles run from $50 to $125 and there are bar snacks out there.

principle.value: Time, place and price range; never promise who sabers or that it happens every week without confirming.

scenarios.title: Like a Sazerac, but lighter
scenarios.guest: I love a Sazerac, but I'd like something lighter tonight.

you.value: Then I'd go one of two ways. Rumors are Flying on our current list keeps the rye: Brennan's own barrel-aged Rittenhouse rye with tart cherry juice, brown sugar syrup and orange bitters, rich but softer, $20.00. Or To Each His Own, Daron Calvados, an apple brandy, with Lillet Blanc and quince liqueur, smooth and fruity, $18.00. And if the Sazerac itself is calling, it's $13.

principle.value: Name what they love about the drink, then offer the same family in a lighter shape with the price of each; say 'current list', because the cocktail list changes with the season.

scenarios.title: What are the luxury cocktails worth?
scenarios.guest: The Roost Bar cocktails cost a lot more. What makes them worth it?

you.value: The bottles and the moment. The Flamingo is Chopin vodka and Monkey 47 gin with dragonfruit, lemon and Taittinger Champagne, $28.00. The Birdcage is a smoked Old Fashioned on Rabbit Hole Dareringer, a bourbon finished in sherry casks, $31.00. The Spoonbill is Hendrick's gin and Cap Corse Mattei Blanc with chive oil, served with a spoon of caviar, $36.00. If you'd rather stay classic, the Sazerac is $13 and Thompson's Dream is $20.

principle.value: Sell the bottles and the theater, never the price: give each drink its one special thing, then name a classic at a lower price so nobody feels pushed.

scenarios.title: A round of brunch cocktails
scenarios.guest: We're celebrating. What should the four of us start with at brunch?

you.value: For a brunch table I'd mix it: a Brandy Milk Punch, our classic eye opener, $12; a Bloody Bull or our Bloody Mary with pickled okra, $13 and $11; and For Sentimental Reasons, sparkling wine with pear purée and allspice dram, $15.00. If anyone isn't drinking, the Personality is zero proof sparkling rosé with tart cherry juice, $16.00. Shall I bring a mix so everyone can taste?

principle.value: Offer a spread across the styles, creamy, savory and sparkling, with one spirit-free choice, and give each price once.

scenarios.title: Not drinking tonight
scenarios.guest: I'm not drinking tonight. What do you have?

you.value: Plenty. The Personality is Wölffer Estate zero proof sparkling rosé with tart cherry juice and brown sugar syrup, fizzy and tart, $16.00; Oh! What It Seemed to Be is a fall sour on Lyre's non-alcoholic agave with fig syrup, lemon and cinnamon syrup, $16.00, non-alcoholic rather than zero; and our Café Glacé de la Maison is chicory cold brew with cardamom-clove syrup, $11. With dessert, our chicory coffee is the classic. And I'll steer you past the dishes cooked with alcohol, like the Foster and the turtle soup.

principle.value: Treat a spirit-free guest as a guest with a drink order: three real drinks with their prices, honesty that Lyre's is under half a percent, and the dishes cooked with alcohol named before they order.

scenarios.title: What is on the children's menu?
scenarios.guest: What can our seven-year-old have, and how much is it?

you.value: Our children's menu is for ten and under, $25.00 for three courses with a drink. At breakfast it's sliced fresh fruit first, then eggs any style with toast and bacon, popcorn shrimp with Brabant potatoes, vanilla French toast with berries and whipped cream, or a grilled cheese with Brabant potatoes, and a scoop of vanilla ice cream to finish. At dinner it's a salami and cheese starter, then fried Gulf shrimp with French fries, buttered noodles with cheese, sautéed Gulf fish with potato and green beans, or a grilled cheese with French fries, and the same ice cream. I'll check today's kid's drink with the bar.

principle.value: Read the card for the meal they are at: the age, the one price and the three-course shape, then the four plates, and confirm the drink rather than promising one.

difference.value: Eggs Hussarde is the classic: housemade English muffin, coffee-cured Canadian bacon, poached eggs, hollandaise and marchand de vin ($27). Eggs Owen is heartier: red wine-braised short rib débris, Creole-spiced potato and a soft-boiled egg with the same two sauces ($32).

ask.value: Do you want the classic Brennan’s egg dish, or something heartier, more like steak and eggs?

difference.value: Turtle soup is 100% turtle meat with brown butter spinach, grated egg and aged Sherry, rich, dark and savory. The gumbo is seafood, shrimp, crab, oysters, with smoky andouille over popcorn rice. Both $13; the breakfast tasting offers either.

ask.value: Are you in the mood for something rich and classic, or seafood with a little smoke?

difference.value: The breakfast/lunch hanger ($38) is Creekstone Prime with smoked potato pavé, a sunny-side-up egg and béarnaise, steak and eggs. The dinner hanger ($42) has housemade Creole spice, Madeira-glazed broccolini, pepita persillade and chili crisp, spicier, with no egg.

ask.value: Mostly a matter of meal, at dinner, ask: “Do you enjoy a little heat? The chili crisp brings some.”

difference.value: Both are flambéed tableside over housemade vanilla ice cream. Bananas Foster (invented here in 1951) is bananas in butter, brown sugar, cinnamon and rum, rich and caramel. Cherries Jubilee is fresh tart black cherries in Luxardo sauce, brighter and fruitier. Cherries Jubilee is not on the dessert menu of 3 October 2026; confirm with a manager before offering it.

ask.value: Would you like something rich and caramelly, or tart and fruity? Before offering the Jubilee, check with a manager: it is not on the current dessert menu.

difference.value: The Louisiana Oysters are the breakfast and lunch starter, $19, cooked in the buttery New Orleans BBQ sauce with pickled collards and a saltine crumble. The Grand Isle Jewel Oysters are the dinner starter, $22, served raw and cold with a preserved Fresno chili mignonette and the raw advisory.

ask.value: Cooked and buttery, or raw and cold?

difference.value: The Pecan Gulf Fish is the breakfast and lunch entrée, $31, with lump crab, pecan bordelaise, cauliflower purée and collards. The Gulf Fish en Papillote is the dinner entrée, $38, steamed in a banana leaf with crab, Castelvetrano olives, tomato, sorghum and Marcona almonds.

ask.value: A rich pecan butter sauce, or the lighter banana leaf parcel with olives and tomato?

difference.value: Old Buttermilk Sky, $18.00, is the fall list's tequila sour: Volcán reposado tequila, fig liqueur, lemon, egg white and cinnamon syrup. Oh! What It Seemed to Be, $16.00, is its spirit-free twin on Temperance, 1946: Lyre's non-alcoholic agave, fig syrup, lemon, egg white and cinnamon syrup.

Rumors are Flying, $20.00, is Brennan's barrel-aged Rittenhouse rye with tart cherry juice, brown sugar syrup and orange bitters. The Personality, $16.00, is spirit-free: Wölffer Estate zero proof sparkling rosé with the same tart cherry juice and brown sugar syrup.

ask.value: The rye drink, or the spirit-free sparkling one?

difference.value: Ralph's Coffee, $8.00, is dark roast coffee with chicory, Frangelico and Nocello under whipped cream. Brennan's Irish Coffee, $12.00, is the same coffee with brown sugar and Tullamore Dew Irish whiskey under whipped cream.

ask.value: With the hazelnut and walnut liqueurs, or with Irish whiskey?

body.value: Invented at Brennan’s in 1951: Owen Brennan challenged his sister Ella and chef Paul Blangé to create a banana dessert (the house's own page and Ralph Brennan credit Ella with Blangé; the commission is also called the Metropolitan Crime Commission), named for Richard Foster, Owen’s friend and chairman of the New Orleans Crime Commission. Flambéed tableside, $14, minimum 2 people per order; 2026 is its 75th year.

Two desserts are flambéed at the table: Bananas Foster and Cherries Jubilee. Chef Kris Padalino (executive chef since June 2025) has said she wants to bring back more tableside cooking, ask at training who performs it (server or captain) and learn the house procedure. Cherries Jubilee is not on the dessert menu of 3 October 2026: confirm with a manager that it is served before offering it.

Breakfast & lunch (Mon-Fri 9 to 2, Sat-Sun 8 to 2): 7 appetizers (including three sweet starters), 8 entrées, 7 sides. Dinner (nightly 6 to 10): 7 appetizers, 6 entrées, 5 sides at $12. One dessert menu, linked from both. Turtle soup, gumbo and the Creole Caesar appear at both meals.

Tasting portions of each course and all listed drinks included: Brandy Milk Punch eye opener → baked apple → turtle soup or seafood gumbo with a Bloody Bull → Eggs Hussarde with Charles Lafitte Brut (4 oz) → petite filet with Châteaumar Côtes du Rhône (4 oz) → Bananas Foster tableside with Congregation Coffee & Chicory. The page says “Celebrating 80 Years in 2026!”

Grand Isle Jewel oysters → Louisiana BBQ lobster → Redfish Véronique → Rohan duck → The Snickers. Wine pairing supplement $120 (4 oz pours): Charles Lafitte Brut, Fichet Mâcon-Igé 2024, Louis Jadot Beaune 1er Cru 2023, Paul Hobbs Coombsville Cabernet 2021, La Tour Vieille Banyuls Reserva.

Menus checked 2026-09-26 and again against the owner’s paste of 3 October 2026; none carries a date. Dinner is a late-summer menu (Creole tomatoes, summer squash, glazed summer vegetables, peaches), and the cocktail list is now the fall list, Billboard Songs from 1946, which replaced Summer Vacations of 1946.

Brennan's first won the Wine Spectator Grand Award in 1983, lost the cellar to Katrina in 2005 when a month without power cooked about 35,000 bottles, and won it back in 2021 after rebuilding to more than 15,000 bottles, with Burgundy and Champagne the deep end of the list; the Wine Spectator listing shows about 3,600 selections and more than 19,000 bottles, deepest in Burgundy, Bordeaux and California. Confirm the award years from the listing at lineup. The live by-the-glass list (Binwise) pours Rare Brut 2012 and Leflaive Mâcon-Verzé by Coravin, plus Inglenook Rubicon 2010 at $70. The restaurant’s own “Cocktails & Wine by the Glass” page shows an older, different glass list (e.g., Drouhin Chablis, Peter Michael, Rare 2013), check the list you’re handed on shift.

Classic eye openers: Bloody Bull $13, Brandy Milk Punch $12, Brennan’s Bloody Mary $11 (pickled okra, spicy beans), Brennan’s Irish Coffee $12. Coffee $11: New Orleans-style with chicory, a single-origin Papua New Guinea from Congregation Coffee, and Café Glacé de la Maison (chicory cold brew, cardamom-clove syrup, orange flower foam). Revive cold-pressed juice $10. Congregation roasts in Algiers; read the single origin from the coffee card on shift rather than naming Papua New Guinea from memory.

Roost Bar & Courtyard, Mon-Fri 2 to 6; Champagne sabering Fridays at 5. Rosé bottles $50 to 125 (Mirabelle to Pommery), bubbly cocktails $12 to 20 (Brennan’s Champagne Cocktail $20), and bar snacks: Creole spiced nuts $6, crawfish meat pies with chive rémoulade $16, fries with pink sauce $8, fried pickles $14, popcorn shrimp $15, cheese board $24, Roost Burger $17. The hours are dated 26 September 2026 and disputed (an older guest description gives Tuesday to Friday 2 to 7): confirm on shift. Sabering has been advertised weekly for about a decade; confirm each Friday with the host stand, and check the courtyard is not privately booked before promising it. Mirabelle is Schramsberg's California sparkling rosé, so say sparkling rosé for the bottom of that range and keep the word Champagne for the Pommery. The bubbly cocktails on the menus of 3 October 2026: Riviera $12.00 (Lillet Blanc, printed Lilet, sparkling wine, lemon), Bodrum $12.00 (rum, pistachio, cream, lime, sparkling water), OBX $12.00 (Gentilly gin, peach, lemon, Elio Perrone Bigaro), Brennan's Champagne Cocktail $20.00 (Champagne, Angostura bitters, demerara sugar cube) and the Chandon Garden Spritz $15.00 (bitter orange liqueur, Chandon Brut sparkling wine).

Temperance, 1946, the spirit-free selections on the menus of 3 October 2026: Personality $16.00 (Wölffer Estate zero proof sparkling rosé, tart cherry juice, brown sugar syrup) and Oh! What It Seemed to Be $16.00 (Lyre's N/A agave, fig syrup, lemon, egg white, cinnamon syrup). Lyre's is labeled under 0.5 percent, so call that one non-alcoholic, not zero; confirm the alcohol figure on the Wölffer label with the bar. The Catalina Island and the Black Hills are off the current menu. Offer the spirit-free drinks to guests who skip the flambé or the milk punch.
Dressy casual; jackets preferred at dinner. No athletic or cut-off shorts, sleeveless or decal T-shirts, hats, or open-toed shoes for men.

Brennan’s opened in 1946 (at 417 Royal Street since 1956) and celebrates 80 years in 2026, with anniversary tasting menus through the year. Owen Brennan died in 1955; the family opened Royal Street in 1956. Brennan's closed in 2013 and reopened in November 2014 under Ralph Brennan and Terry White.

mustKnows.title: Dietary needs: guests note them at the reservation, and the kitchen always confirms

body.value: The kitchen can accommodate most restrictions. Ask guests to note them at the reservation, write them on the ticket, and let the kitchen clear every choice: the kitchen, not the server, says what a dish can do.

Paul Blangé, the chef behind Bananas Foster, led the kitchen until the 1970s. Michael Roussel, who started here in 1956 and trained under Blangé, became executive chef in 1974 and retired in 2005 after 49 years. Lazone Randolph, who began as a dishwasher in 1965, succeeded him in 2005 and gave his name to Chicken Lazone. Slade Rushing ran the kitchen from the 2014 reopening to 2019 and Ryan Hacker from late 2019 to spring 2025. Our executive chef is Kris Padalino, who took over in June 2025 after eight years in this kitchen as pastry chef and executive sous chef; she trained at Le Cordon Bleu in Pasadena and cooked in Los Angeles and Denver before New Orleans.

1795: it was Louisiana's first bank, then the home of Paul Morphy, the chess champion; look for the bank's initials in the balcony ironwork. Owen Brennan opened on Bourbon Street in July 1946 and the house moved here in 1956, after Owen's death in November 1955, with Ella Brennan finding the backing. The family split in November 1973, settled in 1974: Owen's side kept Royal Street, Ella's side took Commander's Palace; Brennan's of Houston belongs to Ella's side, so a guest who ate at Brennan's in Houston ate at a cousin. The house closed on 28 June 2013 and reopened on 25 November 2014 under Ralph Brennan and Terry White after seventeen months of restoration.

Ten turtles were found living in the courtyard during the 2014 renovation and adopted; Slade Rushing named them for sauces: Béchamel, Hollandaise, Espagnole, Tomate and Velouté, then Rémoulade, Ravigote, Bordelaise, Mignonette and Cocktail, the only male. Their return to the fountain in 2015 began the annual Slowest Second Line on Earth. Say it before the guest asks: the turtle soup is not the turtles.

Our by-the-glass list in the pack runs to twenty-two wines: fifteen glass pours, from $14 up to the $75 Rare, the Argyle Brut and the Barbera d'Asti new on the current menu among them; an $80 half-bottle of Mosel Auslese the current menu no longer prints, a lineup question; and six wines poured only as part of the tasting menus. If a guest wants one of the tasting wines on its own, ask before promising it. Check the list you are handed on shift: the Binwise list and the menu differ on a few prices and vintages.

Our wine director is Sam Bortugno, an Advanced Sommelier, in post since September 2023; confirm at lineup that he is on the floor tonight and how to call a sommelier to a table. Braithe Gill is beverage director for the Ralph Brennan Restaurant Group, a certified sommelier and a 2026 James Beard semifinalist; the research also recorded her as Braithe Tidwell, who led the program when the Grand Award was regained in 2021, so do not call her the wine director.

mustKnows.title: The Wine Room and private events

body.value: The Wine Room is our smallest private room, seating 16, in the old carriage house and stables beside the cellar, with a sixteen foot table milled from one sinker cypress; bookings go through the events office on 504-934-3376, with a minimum that depends on the date. Nine bookable spaces, seated and reception: King's 36 and 40, Queen's 24 and 30, Havana 60 and 75, Morphy 12 and 12, Chanteclair 100 and 160, Roost Bar 20 and 30, Audubon 50 and 60, Wine Room 16 and 16, Courtyard 50 and 75; events from 15 to 500. For private parties, corkage is $25 a bottle, a magnum $50 counting as two, six bottles at most; the dining room policy is not published, ask a manager.
Reservations are on OpenTable, open 60 days ahead; parties larger than six ring 504-525-9711.

Royal Street is a pedestrian mall from 11 in the morning, so there is no drop off at the door at lunch; the street is open to cars when breakfast opens and all evening. We validate parking at two garages, 535 Chartres and 716 Iberville, for up to three hours; check the current rates and whether valet is on tonight with the host stand, since the two readings of the FAQ disagree on valet.

Christmas Eve: breakfast and lunch à la carte, dinner 5:30 to 9 with a three course $85 menu. New Year's Eve: breakfast and lunch à la carte, dinner 6 to 10 à la carte. The year is unconfirmed; re-read each season. Réveillon proper is advertised at the sister house Ralph's on the Park; Brennan's frames Christmas Eve as its holiday dinner.
The group runs Brennan's, Napoleon House, Red Fish Grill, Ralph's on the Park, Cafe NOMA, Jazz Kitchen Coastal Grill and Patio, and Beignets Expressed.

mustKnows.title: Who does what on the floor

body.value: Brennan's has captains; staff train for months before cooking Bananas Foster tableside, and a new server does not flame a pan before sign off. Erick Schmitt is general manager per the house's 2026 team directory; confirm the spelling on the page. Who performs the flambé, the Friday sabrage, the Chateaubriand carving, the papillote opening and the Coravin pours, and how the floor is organized, are lineup questions.

For children ten and under, at breakfast and at dinner; the web card read 3 October 2026 prints every item at $25.00, confirm on the live card. Breakfast: Eggs Any Style with Toast and Bacon; Popcorn Shrimp with Brabant Potatoes; Vanilla French Toast with Fresh Berries and Whipped Cream; Grilled Cheese Sandwich with Brabant Potatoes, each with a kid's drink, sliced fresh fruit first and a scoop of vanilla ice cream after. Dinner: Fried Gulf Shrimp with French Fries; Buttered Noodles with Cheese; Sautéed Gulf Fish with Potato and Green Beans; Grilled Cheese Sandwich with French Fries, each with a kid's drink, a salami and cheese starter and vanilla ice cream; tell parents the starter is salami and cheese, not fruit. High chairs are available. The dress code states no exemption for children: say the house asks for dressy casual and leave enforcement to the host. The guide never mentions the card; it is a web fact.

mustKnows.title: The Roost Bar and the cocktail list

body.value: The current list, Billboard Songs from 1946, celebrating 80 years at Brennan's, as the owner pasted the menus on 3 October 2026: For Sentimental Reasons $15.00 (allspice dram, pear purée, sparkling wine), Prisoner of Love $16.00 (gin, Earl Grey tea, clarified heavy cream, orange flower water), Rumors are Flying $20.00 (Brennan's barrel-aged Rittenhouse rye, tart cherry juice, brown sugar syrup, orange bitters), To Each His Own $18.00 (Daron Fine Calvados, Lillet Blanc, quince liqueur), Old Buttermilk Sky $18.00 (Volcán reposado tequila, fig liqueur, lemon, egg white, cinnamon syrup) and Five Minutes More $20.00 (Cathead mandarin vodka, Green Chartreuse, Licor 43, lemon); spirit-free under Temperance, 1946: Personality $16.00 and Oh! What It Seemed to Be $16.00. It replaces Summer Vacations of 1946: the Yellowstone, Miami Beach, Niagara Falls, Havana and Acapulco are off the menu. The Sazerac Selections stand: Classic Sazerac $13.00, Thompson's Dream $20.00 and Origin Story $40.00 (the menu spells it Orgin Story). The Roost Bar's luxury cocktails, served only there and not on the paste, so confirm them on shift: Flamingo $28 (Chopin vodka, Monkey 47 gin, dragonfruit, lemon, Taittinger La Française Champagne), Birdcage $31 (a smoked Old Fashioned on Rabbit Hole Dareringer bourbon, Angostura, orange, cherry) and Spoonbill $36 (Hendrick's gin, Cap Corse Mattei Blanc quinquina, chive oil, a spoon of caviar); measures, glass and garnish to confirm on shift.
On 6 April 2026 we threw a courtyard party for the dessert's 75th birthday: a Champagne sabering, free tastes for the first 75 guests, a flame competition and the crowning of a Banana King.

Breakfast and lunch run 9 to 2 on weekdays and 8 to 2 at weekends, dinner is every night 6 to 10, and Bubbles at Brennan's happy hour is weekdays 2 to 6 in the Roost Bar and Courtyard, with Champagne sabered on Fridays at 5. Dress is dressy casual, jackets preferred at dinner, and no athletic shorts, sleeveless shirts, hats or open toed shoes for gentlemen. Dated 3 October 2026.

mustKnows.title: Café Brûlot is a cake, not a drink, on today's menus

body.value: The only Brûlot item is the Café Brûlot Coffee Cake. Café Brûlot Diabolique, the flamed brandy and chicory coffee, was devised at Antoine's by Jules Alciatore around 1890; the house served it in the family era and the cookbook carries a recipe, but it is on no current menu and only two things are flamed at the table, both desserts. Do not offer it as a drink until the house confirms it.

On the dessert menu of 3 October 2026, at breakfast, lunch and dinner. Dessert cocktails: Floating in South Africa $15.00 (Amarula cream liqueur, housemade vanilla bean ice cream, Abita root beer), Apple Crumble $15.00 (bourbon, apple cider, butterscotch schnapps, maple, cinnamon, lemon, black walnut bitters) and Banane au Chocolat $16.00 (crème de banana, crème de cocoa, Pedro Ximénez sherry). Coffee cocktails: Espresso Martini $16.00 (chicory, vodka, Frangelico, Kahlua), Ralph's Coffee $8.00 (dark roast coffee with chicory, Frangelico, Nocello, whipped cream) and Brennan's Irish Coffee $12.00, which is also an eye opener at breakfast and lunch. The Dulce de Leche, the dessert cocktail of the summer list, is off the current menu.

askAtLineup.question: Which Champagne is poured with the Eggs Hussarde on the Traditional Breakfast today? The guide and the current menu both print Charles Lafitte Brut, 4 oz: confirm the bottle open.
Is the house Champagne $28 or $30 a glass today, and is the bottle a Brennan's labeled Piper-Heidsieck Essentiel or a bespoke blend? What is the dosage and disgorgement date?

Which Rare vintage is open under the Coravin Sparkling stopper: 2012, as the live list prints, or the 2013 Millésime on the restaurant's drinks page? And which device and log procedure does the bar use for it and for the Leflaive?
Taste the open Berres Riesling and record the label ABV: the importer's sheet says off-dry (20.7 g/l residual sugar, 11.5%). Print one answer; six pairings hinge on it.

Are the Banyuls and the Jadot Beaune poured à la carte, at breakfast and at dinner, and at what price per 2 to 3 oz? If not, the coffee cake, the Cherries Jubilee and the Snickers are coffee only, and the Chateaubriand's second choice becomes the Moulin d'Issan.
Can the Dr. Hermann Auslese be rung as a single 2 to 3 oz pour at a glass price, or only as the $80 half-bottle?

Which duck plate is on the dinner tasting tonight: the roasted Rohan breast with cane syrup-glazed peaches and candied hazelnuts, as the guide and the current menu both print? Confirm the garnish, and what temperature the kitchen serves it.

Which white is poured with the lobster on the dinner tasting tonight? The guide and the current menu both print Fichet Mâcon-Igé 2024, with Louis Jadot 1er Cru Beaune 2023 on the redfish and La Tour Vieille Reserva Banyuls on the Snickers: confirm the bottles open.
Are the $80 dinner tasting and the $120 pairing supplement correct as printed? May a guest swap included pours for the spirit-free drinks at no charge, or decline a pour and reduce the price?
Bubbles at Brennan's: are the days and hours still Monday to Friday 2 to 6, who sabers on Fridays at 5, which bottle, and may guests take part?

Who performs the tableside flambé (server, captain or a dedicated cart person), how long is the training, and is there a sign off before a new server lights a pan? Does the house still dust cinnamon into the flame?
Does the cart build for Bananas Foster use banana liqueur as well as rum, as the published recipe does, or rum only as the menu prints? Which rum?
Is Bananas Foster the most ordered item on the menu, as the guide said, and does the restaurant want servers to say so? The published figure elsewhere is about 35,000 pounds of bananas a year.
The house's preferred telling of the Bananas Foster origin: Owen challenging Blangé, or Ella and Blangé adapting their mother's dish? And which name for the commission?
Does the house tell Eggs Hussarde as created here by Paul Blangé? Confirm the house wording before servers say 'created here'.
The Classic Sazerac build: sugar cube or syrup, dash count, lemon peel in or out, the glass, and whether the bar will build it on a large cube if a guest asks for it on the rocks.
How is the marchand de vin built tonight: the house recipe with ham, mushroom and onion, or a plain shallot and red wine reduction? No house recipe page is published.

What exactly is in the New Orleans BBQ sauce on the Louisiana Oysters and the BBQ Lobster (Worcestershire, anchovy, smoked chili butter), how are the oysters cooked, and how many per order? Does the 'nduja carry real heat?

Does the dining room turtle soup follow the published recipe (all turtle, thickened with flour, beef stock, finished with egg, spinach, lemon and sherry)? Is the sherry added in the kitchen or tableside? Who is the current turtle supplier?
Does the dining room gumbo follow the published recipe (a flour roux, okra, tomato, filé)? Is the seafood finished to order?
Is the published hollandaise (butter, egg yolks, lemon, Champagne vinegar, Crystal, cayenne, sea salt) the one served on the Hussarde and the Owen?
Are the Eggs Sardou artichokes breaded in panko as the published recipe has them (two artichokes, two eggs, Parmesan creamed spinach), and is the breakfast creamed spinach side the same preparation?
Brabant potatoes: how are they finished (garlic butter and parsley) and in which fryer? The guide prints bra-BAHNT; does the floor say it that way, or bra-BAHN or bruh-BANT?
Is Maggie's Mushrooms sourced from Mushroom Maggie's Farm at St Francisville, and what are tonight's varieties and preparation (butter, stock)?
Which Luxardo product is in the Cherries Jubilee sauce and which spirit is flamed at the table? Can a single Cherries Jubilee be ordered?
Is the Blackened Tofu made with oil rather than butter, and do the rice grits use stock, so that it can be sold as vegan? Is the blackening blend cayenne based?
Is tonight's pecan bordelaise garlic butter or red wine based? It decides white versus Pinot on the Pecan Gulf Fish. What is today's Gulf fish?
Is the Chateaubriand carved tableside or in the kitchen, and what cooking time should we quote? Is the papillote opened at the table, and by whom?
Is Eggs Owen named for Owen Brennan, and does the house want servers to tell that story?

Does the Gainey Chardonnay read fresh rather than oaky, and which appellation and tier is on the bottle (Sta. Rita Hills or Santa Ynez Valley)? If fresh, the cellar dossier would lead with it on both crab dishes and keep the Leflaive as the step up.
Which Loire appellation is on the Domaine Durand label, and who are the producer and importer of the Damien Martin Bourgogne? Is the Minuty still the 2024 and the Pazo das Bruxas the 2025?

Which vintage of the Châteaumar Cuvée Vincent is open for the breakfast tasting (the current menu prints 2023), and is it the Côtes du Rhône rather than the estate's Châteauneuf of the same name? What is the printed 2023 blend of the Moulin d'Issan and the 2024 blend of the Durban?

How is the Inglenook Rubicon 2010 preserved between $70 pours, how far ahead is it stood upright, and is it still the 2010? Is the Paul Hobbs the Coombsville appellation bottling and is it decanted at the start of service?
Which Charles Lafitte cuvée is poured on the tastings, can it be poured à la carte, and at what price?
Which Grand Award years does the Wine Spectator listing give (1983 to 2005, regained 2021), is the award current this year, and how many bottles and selections are in the cellar now?
Where is the Wine Room and where are the bottles kept (the scripts said 'upstairs' and 'the cellar'), who is on the floor as sommelier tonight, and how does a server summon one?
Is valet offered, at which services and at what price, and are the two validated garages (535 Chartres and 716 Iberville) still current?

Has the glass list, the dinner menu or the cocktail list changed since 26 September 2026? The guide expected a fall change; the cocktails page snippet priced Bananas Foster at $12 against the guide's $14.

Which Luxardo cherries, which whiskey in the bread pudding caramel, does the vanilla ice cream contain egg, is the Snickers Bavarian set with gelatin, and does the nougat ice cream carry nuts besides the peanuts? Kitchen questions for the dessert cards.

Which pronunciations does the house use: hoo-SARD or hoo-ZARD for Hussarde, TAH-so or TASS-oh, bra-BAHNT as the guide prints it or bra-BAHN or bruh-BANT, and how does the kitchen say Tien Dat and Nueske's?
Does the Creole Caesar dressing contain raw egg or anchovy beside the smoked oysters, and are the oysters smoked in house?
Which supplier provides the farm-raised Louisiana turtle for the Turtle Soup today? Confirm the current supplier with the kitchen before naming one to a guest.
The children's menu: is every plate still $25.00 at breakfast and at dinner, what is today's kid's drink, and how many high chairs are on hand?
Are the two premium Sazeracs (Thompson’s Dream and Origin Story) rung under the Sazerac section or on the luxury page?
Who is the general manager tonight, and how is the name spelled? The house site’s team page lists Erick Schmitt; confirm the spelling on the page before a server uses it.

Holiday services: are Christmas Eve (breakfast and lunch a la carte, dinner 5:30 to 9 with a three course menu) and New Year’s Eve (breakfast and lunch a la carte, dinner 6 to 10 a la carte) as the house site printed, and for which year? Re read the page each season.

Are the sourcing names printed on the menus still current: Creekstone Farms, Vital Farms, D’Artagnan, Two Brooks, Leidenheimer, Nueske’s, Tien Dat tofu and Maggie’s Mushrooms? Confirm each at lineup before a server names it.
Is the Flamingo ($28.00) still on the Luxury Roost Bar page, and what are its measures, glass and garnish?
Is the Birdcage ($31.00) still on the Luxury Roost Bar page, how is it smoked, and what are its glass and garnish?
Is the Spoonbill ($36.00) still on the Luxury Roost Bar page, which caviar and how much comes on the spoon, and what is the glass?
Thompson's Dream ($20): still poured, the measures, the Willett bottling and its proof, and whether the name honors Thompson Willett?
Origin Story ($40): still poured, which Dudognon expression, who barrel-ages the Peychaud's and in what cask, and the measures?
Brennan's Bloody Mary ($11): is the mix the Bloody Bull's housemade mix, which vodka, and how hot is it?
Is each coffee $11 (one $11 is printed before all three), and is the chicory coffee the Brennan's private blend from Congregation at every meal?
Which single origin is Congregation roasting for us today? The guide printed a Papua New Guinea; read it off the coffee card.
Revive Cold-Pressed Juice ($10.00): the menu now prints Strawberry, Apple and Pineapple. Which of the three are in today?
For Sentimental Reasons ($15.00): which sparkling wine and which allspice dram, the measures, the glass and the garnish?
Prisoner of Love ($16.00): which gin, how the bar clarifies the heavy cream, the measures, the glass and the garnish?
Rumors are Flying ($20.00): who barrel-aged the Rittenhouse rye for Brennan's, in what cask and for how long; is it served up or over ice, and in what glass?
To Each His Own ($18.00): which quince liqueur, the measures, the glass and the garnish?
Old Buttermilk Sky ($18.00): which fig liqueur, how the bar prepares the egg white and whether it can be left out, the glass and the garnish?
Five Minutes More ($20.00): the measures, the glass and the garnish?
Personality ($16.00): what alcohol figure does the Wölffer Estate Zero Proof Sparkling Rosé label give, and what are the glass and the garnish?
Oh! What It Seemed to Be ($16.00): which Lyre's agave (Blanco or Reserva), how the bar prepares the egg white and whether it can be left out, the glass and the garnish?
Floating in South Africa ($15.00): how is it built and served (glass, spoon or straw), and can the bar make a plain root beer float for a child?
Apple Crumble ($15.00): is it served hot or cold, which bourbon, and what are the glass and the garnish?
Banane au Chocolat ($16.00): which crème de banana, crème de cocoa and Pedro Ximénez sherry, and what are the glass and the garnish?
Espresso Martini ($16.00): is the chicory our chicory coffee, espresso or a chicory liqueur, does it carry caffeine, and what are the glass and the garnish?
Ralph's Coffee ($8.00): is it served hot, in which glass, and is the coffee the same dark roast with chicory as the Irish Coffee?
Ralph's Coffee: who is it named for, and does the house want servers to tell the story? Until a manager says, servers tell none.
Riviera ($12.00): which sparkling wine, the measures, the glass and the garnish? The menu spells the Lillet as Lilet.
Bodrum ($12.00): which rum, how the pistachio goes in (a syrup, an orgeat or a liqueur), the glass and the garnish?
OBX ($12.00): who distills the Gentilly gin, how the peach goes in, the glass and the garnish?
OBX: the Elio Perrone Bigaro, how sweet it runs, its grapes and its strength, for a guest who asks?
Chandon Garden Spritz ($15.00): which bitter orange liqueur, is it built at the bar or poured ready made, which Chandon Brut, and what are the glass and the garnish?
Brennan's Champagne Cocktail ($20.00): the menu now prints Champagne, Angostura Bitters and a Demerara Sugar Cube; which Champagne is poured, in what glass, and is there a garnish?
Billboard Songs from 1946: when a guest asks who sang a song on the list, does the house want servers to name a recording, and which one? Until then, servers name none.

Which Sauvignon Blanc is open by the glass: the Famille Durand Val de Loire 2024 the current menu prints, or the Domaine Durand Loire Valley 2025 on Binwise? Is it fermented in steel with no oak, as the guide said of the 2025?
The current menu prints the Damien Martin at $18.00 and the Durban at $19.00 a glass; Binwise still prints $17 and $18. Which price rings tonight?
Which Moulin d'Issan vintage is open by the glass: the 2021 the current menu prints, or the 2023 on Binwise? Both head it a Cabernet Sauvignon blend: what is the 2021's blend?

The Dr. Hermann Erdener Prälat Auslese 2014 half-bottle ($80) is on the Binwise list (bin 31122) but not on the current Wines by the Glass page: is it still offered by the half-bottle with dessert and the sweet starters?

Is the La Miraja Le Masche Barbera d'Asti 2023 poured by the glass tonight at $16.00, how is it aged, how is Le Masche said, and is there a bottle price? It is on the current menu but not on the Binwise list.

The Birthday Bubbles half bottles and large formats: which are in stock tonight (Binwise lists no Drappier or Paul Bara half bottle), who opens the magnums and the double magnum, and are they iced ahead or to order?

The five rosé bottles on the Bubbles at Brennan's page print a happy hour price beside the original: are they sold outside Bubbles hours, and at the original price? Only the Taittinger Prestige Rosé is on the Binwise list; which are in stock?
Cherries Jubilee is not on the dessert menu the owner pasted on 3 October 2026: is it still served, at which meals, and at what price? Until a manager says, confirm it before offering it.
The Birthday Bubbles half bottles and large formats and the five Bubbles rosés: the menus print no blend for these twelve bottles. What grapes go into each, for a guest who asks?

The Argyle Brut 2022 is printed by the glass at $15.00 as Vintage Brut on the glass list and as Brut on the Birthday Bubbles page and Binwise: is it one bottle, what is its grape blend, and how is it made?

history.value: Owen Brennan opened the restaurant on Bourbon Street in July 1946, and it has been at 417 Royal Street since 1956. Owen died in November 1955, before the move; Ella Brennan found the backing and the family opened Royal Street in 1956. The building dates from 1795, was the first bank in Louisiana and later the home of Paul Morphy, the chess champion; the bank's initials survive in the balcony ironwork. The family split in November 1973, settled in 1974: Owen's widow Maude and sons Pip, Jimmy and Ted kept Royal Street, and Ella's side took Commander's Palace. Brennan's closed in June 2013 and reopened in November 2014 under Ralph Brennan and Terry White after a restoration of the whole house. Paul Blange, the first chef, created Bananas Foster and Eggs Hussarde; Michael Roussel, Lazone Randolph, Slade Rushing and Ryan Hacker followed him, and Kris Padalino has led the kitchen since June 2025. 2026 is the 80th year.
